record.paper_title: Open questions regarding the arrow of time
record.original_question: Why do electromagnetic absorbers, and more generally physical absorptive processes, pick out only one temporal direction? In the case of retarded versus advanced Maxwell fields, if absorbers and thermalization can account for retarded shadows and the absence of incoming high-frequency radiation, what explains the fact that all absorbers absorb in the same time direction rather than admitting the time-reversed alternative with advanced correlations?

evidence.quote: This asymmetry may be understood as a consequence of the presence of absorbers (including the early radiation era of our universe).
But why do all absorbers absorb in one and the same direction of time only?
This absence of advanced correlations is even “probable”, while the low-entropy initial condition that leads to retarded correlations – such as a special initial µ-space distribution ρµ – is not.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider classical electrodynamics governed by the time-symmetric Maxwell equations, which admit, for any prescribed source current, both retarded Green-function solutions (in which the field at a spacetime point depends on the source on its past light cone) and advanced Green-function solutions (in which the field depends on the source on its future light cone). Empirically, all observed macroscopic radiation phenomena are described by purely retarded fields: emitters cast "retarded shadows" on absorbers in their causal future, and there is a generic absence of incoming, coherently focused high-frequency radiation that would correspond to advanced correlations.

A standard partial explanation invokes absorbers (matter, including the radiation-dominated early universe) which thermalize incoming coherent radiation and thereby suppress advanced-type correlations. However, this explanation presupposes that absorbers act in a single, common temporal direction.

Provide a derivation, from time-symmetric microscopic dynamics together with admissible cosmological/boundary conditions, of the following fact: every physical absorber in the observable universe absorbs in one and the same direction of time, rather than the time-reversed alternative in which absorption (equivalently, anti-thermalization producing advanced coherent outgoing radiation) occurs in the opposite temporal direction. In particular, identify the structural ingredient — be it an initial low-entropy condition, a cosmological boundary condition, a statistical-mechanical principle, or otherwise — that selects a single global absorptive arrow of time and explain why this selection is "probable" (typical) rather than requiring a fine-tuned hypothesis comparable to a special low-entropy initial micro-state.
artifact.category_tag: Arrow of time and absorber theory
artifact.status_search_result: The question of why all absorbers act in the same temporal direction is a long-standing foundational problem connected to Wheeler-Feynman absorber theory and the cosmological arrow of time. Recent literature (2020s philosophy-of-physics and arXiv preprints, including discussions of time-symmetric quantum mechanics and generalized absorber theory) continues to debate the issue, with no consensus derivation from time-symmetric dynamics alone; explanations typically invoke either a special cosmological boundary condition or a thermodynamic/low-entropy past hypothesis, both of which remain contested.

status_evidence.title: The hidden arrow of electromagnetic radiation: unmasking advanced waves
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses unresolved status of advanced vs. retarded asymmetry and the role of absorbers in selecting an electromagnetic arrow of time.
status_evidence.claim: The electromagnetic arrow of time and the asymmetry of absorption remain actively debated foundational problems.

status_evidence.title: Time Symmetry, Retrocausality and the Emergent Arrow of Time
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) treatment of how a global arrow of time may emerge in time-symmetric quantum frameworks, indicating no settled answer.
status_evidence.claim: The unified absorptive arrow of time is still being investigated as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: The philosophical underpinning of the absorber theory of radiation
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews persistent foundational difficulties with absorber-based explanations of the radiation arrow.
status_evidence.claim: Explanations of why all absorbers share one temporal direction remain unsettled.
